meta.matchSemantics: Match on roleSignature within the v3 same-color bar (all four roles), never exact hex equality. meta.gatePolicy: Every entry here has a bad standing grade under the recency rule, and blocks integration when a v3 output matches it. The sole exception is contested: true — conflicting grades at an identical timestamp, which recency cannot decide; those warn rather than block. Palettes whose latest grade is strong or acceptable are absent from this file entirely, even if an earlier comparison graded them bad; they live in endorsements.json or acceptable.json instead.
meta.recencyRule: Latest-timestamped grade wins (reviewer decision 2026-08-02). Where the same artwork and the same exact palette were graded more than once, the most recent grade is the pair's standing verdict; earlier grades are history, not live contradictions. Only conflicting grades sharing an identical timestamp stay unresolved, and those warn rather than block.

unrecoverable.notes: Flo, scoping the zero-contrast rule (follow-up to cs2-batch 07d4cb): a mid-gradient APCA zero-crossing is not the same thing as exact-zero contrast between foreground and surface/background. The crossing is a single thin line orthogonal to the gradient; the role pairs are flat colors occupying large areas, so zero holds everywhere. Consequence: the hue-conditional tolerance for sign flips (birdsofprey) applies only to thin gradient crossings, never to flat role-pair contrast. A flat fg/surface pair at ~zero APCA is invalid regardless of hue separation.

unrecoverable.notes: Flo, on the endorsed teal #0e4355 / oxblood #6b141a gradient for 093ce4: endpoint extension will NOT pass through the needed dark midpoint. The midpoint is an extra color that must be added because the straight OKLab interpolation between the endpoints passes through a color that doesn't feel like part of the artwork. Two distinct mechanisms: (1) endpoint extension outward along the ramp; (2) detect when the straight line between endpoints crosses colors the artwork doesn't contain, and insert a source-supported midpoint to bend the ramp back onto artwork colors. (2) is the mechanism behind both this palette and the thrice-asked 09d178 rich gradient.

evidence.label: ra2-off
evidence.notes:
These proposed palettes don't really match the artwork. The artwork has a mostly dark background, fully black on the outside and a dark blue to blue gradient in the middle. It also has white drawings and a bright red symbol. I think the confusion might come from the fact that on top of the white drawing there is black text. So it looks like the foreground should be some sort of black or dark blue.

I think a better palette would actually use a white as the foreground. The red symbol's color could be used as the accent, and then background and surface could be black and blue, possibly with a gradient 

At the very least, if we keep this white background, we need to have the accent represent the red symbol's color because right now the palettes look pretty much just black and white with a slight blue tint, which doesn't fit this artwork
